items.title: Jim Galloway interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: I’m still a good friend of Red Richards

ctx.x: Cool. Was it any kind of culture shock at all or was it fairly—

Oh yeah, a little bit, a little bit. The first shock was the very first night I arrived. Again, at that time in Glasgow for example, you didn’t go into a bar to hear jazz. They didn’t have music in bars as they have here. And so on my first night in Toronto I was on Yonge Street which is the main drag, and there’s this place I see called the Colonial Tavern. And so I go in there and I literally stopped in my tracks because on the bandstand there was Vic Dickinson, Buster Bailey, Herman Autrey, Red Richards on…
That was a pretty good affirmation of your decision though I guess. Hey, I did the right thing. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
